name: Estrogen/hormone skin theories (DHT acne)
lead: Hormone-and-skin theories in looksmaxxing communities center on the idea that androgens such as DHT, and drugs that change hormone levels such as anabolic steroids, drive acne, and that estrogen or anti-androgen approaches can offset it. Dermatology references do link androgens to acne: testosterone, DHT and DHEA increase sebum production, and DHT is described as the main hormonal driver of sebum [1].

Research on acne caused by steroids exists mainly for corticosteroids and in clinical settings such as transplant patients. A 1989 review described steroid acne as increasingly common with organ transplantation and cancer treatment [2].

paras: Wikipedia notes that androgens and IGF-1 appear necessary for acne, that acne does not develop in complete androgen insensitivity syndrome, and that conditions with high androgens such as polycystic ovary syndrome can cause acne [1]. Anabolic-androgenic steroids and testosterone replacement can cause acne [1].
Hormonal treatments listed include combined oral contraceptives, spironolactone and topical clascoterone approved in 2020 [1].

Steroid acne is a folliculitis that can result from systemic or topical steroids; a 1998 study compared it with Pityrosporum folliculitis and assessed antifungal drugs [3]. A 1989 review described its development through follicular changes leading to microcomedones and rupture, with exact pathogenesis uncertain [2].

Registered trials include a study of clascoterone for steroid-related acne in transgender men receiving masculinizing hormone therapy [4], a finasteride trial in severe nodulocystic acne [5], and an oral contraceptive trial in acne with over 1,300 participants [6]. No results are summarized in the sources available here. No studies of looksmaxxing estrogen use for acne were found.

card.summary: Forum theories tying acne to DHT, steroids and estrogen; androgens are linked to acne in dermatology, but looksmaxxing-specific claims lack dedicated studies.
card.note: Hormone-altering approaches carry medical risks; no studies of the community protocols found.

quick.overview:
Forum discussion links acne to DHT and steroids and proposes hormone-based fixes. Dermatology literature supports a role for androgens in acne.

The specific forum protocols have not been studied.
quick.mechanism: Androgens such as DHT increase sebum production, which is associated with acne.
quick.risks: Steroid use can cause acne; hormonal drugs have their own risks and are clinician-managed.
